description:
**Foundation ticket. No predecessors. Read the deck (`tmp/tui_react_proposal.html`)
sections 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 10 before starting.**

**Read first (existing implementation that the new modules will live
beside):**
- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/component.ex` (current Component
  behaviour — will be augmented, not replaced, in this ticket).
- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/render_context.ex` (existing
  RenderContext — kept verbatim, threads through paint).
- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/wrap_ansi.ex` (visible-width and
  truncation logic — paint reuses these).
- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/renderer.ex` (downstream consumer —
  not modified here, but understand its inputs: a list of binaries +
  optional cursor_seq).

**New modules to land (suggested layout):**
- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/vdom.ex` — the VNode struct
  definitions: %VText{}, %VLines{}, %VFlow{}, %VRow{}, %VBox{},
  %VZone{}, %VMemo{}, %VHole{}, %VCursor{}.
- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/vdom/line_buf.ex` — LineBuf as
  {iolist_rev, line_iolist_rev, visible_width, line_count, cursor_or_nil}
  with `push/2`, `push_many/3`, `flush_line/2`, `mark_cursor/2`,
  `finalize/1` returning `{iodata, cursor_or_nil}`.
- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/vdom/paint.ex` — `paint/3`
  multi-head dispatching on VNode struct; `paint_kids/3` and
  `paint_inline_kids/3` walk children-as-iodata.
- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/compat.ex` — wraps any legacy
  `Component.render(state, width) :: [binary()]` (or transcript-shaped
  `Component.render(state, ctx) :: {state, lines, frame_ms}`) as a
  `%VLines{}` leaf so existing components are paintable unchanged
  while migrations are in flight.

**Memo cell shape:** `{iodata, visible_width, cursor_offset_or_nil}`.
On VMemo cache hit, painter splices iodata into the LineBuf and
applies `cursor_offset` (line + column delta within the subtree)
to the running position so cursor coordinates survive cache hits.

**Four framework rules surfaced by §13 worked example. All four MUST
ship in this ticket — every downstream conversion depends on them:**

  1. **Children as iodata.** `%VFlow{children}` and `%VRow{children}`
     accept a child that is either a single VNode or a (possibly
     nested) list of children — same shape iodata uses for bytes.
     The painter walks via `paint_kids/3` recursing into both list
     cells and VNode cells without ever materializing a flat list.
     Component code drops a list of memos straight into a VFlow
     alongside scalar children — no `++`, no `flat_map`. Test:
     a VFlow with a 100-element list child paints in one pass with
     zero list-allocation churn.

  2. **`%VMemo{thunk}` may return any VNode**, including a list /
     VFlow / nested-list shape. Per-block memoization (markdown,
     d06.10) commits one paragraph at a time, each becomes a VMemo;
     the thunk must be allowed to return list-shaped children.
     Test: a memo whose thunk returns a 5-element list survives
     cache hit/miss correctly.

  3. **Hook-cell values are stored by identity, never deep-compared.**
     Components hold large structs (e.g. %MdRender{}) in cells;
     the reconciler treats `cell_value === previous_cell_value` as
     the only "unchanged" signal. Setter calls are the only way to
     mark a cell dirty. Note: this is a *contract* the reconciler
     in d06.2 must honor — this ticket only documents it; tests
     for it land in d06.2.

  4. **Setters called during render fold into the same paint pass**
     (React's "derived state from props" pattern). No second-paint
     scheduled when a render function calls a setter from its own
     body. Same as #3: contract the reconciler must honor; tests
     in d06.2.

**Compat adapter behaviour.** Wraps `module.render(state, width)` and
`module.render(state, ctx)` callsites so a legacy component appears
as a `%VLines{lines: list_of_binaries}` leaf with visible-width
metadata stamped at construction (computed via
`OctoPi.TUI.WrapAnsi.visible_width/1`). The adapter is the bridge
that lets every other migration ticket land independently. Lives
behind a feature flag `:octo_pi_tui_vdom?` defaulting to `false`
so opt-in tests can exercise the new path without breaking existing
flows; flag is removed in d06.8.

**Telemetry:** emit `[:octo_pi_tui, :vdom, :paint]` with measurements
`%{nodes_visited: int, memo_hits: int, memo_misses: int, line_count:
int, byte_count: int, duration: int_ns}` and metadata `%{frame:
int}`. Wire into the existing `RenderTelemetry` module pattern —
read `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/render_telemetry.ex` for the
shape.

**Hard rules (apply to every render-path file you write here):**
- No `++`, no `flat_map`, no `List.flatten` in render or paint code.
- Multi-head pattern matching, not top-level `case`/`if`/`cond` on
  args (per `feedback_pattern_matching` memory).
- Use `Jason.OrderedObject` if any paint code emits JSON (it shouldn't,
  but flagged for completeness — per `feedback_jason_ordered_object`).
- Never `Process.sleep` in tests (per `feedback_no_process_sleep_in_tests`).
- Add a Credo check (or a simple test file) that greps
  `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui` for `++` in component render
  code; failing that test means a future agent slipped a list-concat
  into the hot path.

**Acceptance:**
- New modules compile, dialyze, and are unit-tested.
- Test fixtures cover: border math (VBox), zone welding (VZone — open
  prepended to first painted line, close+final appended to last;
  empty-zone case emits all three on the single line), padding
  (padding_x and padding_y both work), memo hit/miss including
  VMemo-returns-list and VFlow-with-nested-list-children, cursor
  stamping through nested VBox padding offsets, hook-cell identity
  comparison (struct-with-same-fields-but-different-identity counts
  as changed).
- Compat adapter test: a legacy `Components.Header` (the existing
  module, used as a fixture) paints identically when wrapped vs.
  when called directly.
- Performance smoke: paint a 200-line VFlow at width 80 in <2ms on
  a fresh-cache run, <500µs on an all-memo-hit run. Failing this
  bar means the hot-path rules above were violated.
title: VDom core: VNode types, LineBuf, paint phase, Compat adapter behind feature flag
